headline: Injectable hydrogel from University at Buffalo could keep arthritis drugs working for weeks

words.def_en: A disease that causes painful stiff joints
words.example_en: For English learners, this health story connects words like injection, lubrication, and symptom with a real attempt to make arthritis care last longer.

words.def_en: A water-based gel that can hold and release drugs
words.example_en: Scientists at the University at Buffalo say a new injectable hydrogel could change how osteoarthritis is treated.

words.def_en: A place where two bones meet and move
words.example_en: ScienceDaily reports that the material starts as a liquid, then turns into a smooth semisolid depot inside the joint at body temperature.

words.def_en: A slippery layer that reduces friction
words.example_en: The gel also improves lubrication, which could help stiff, painful knees move more smoothly during daily activity.

words.def_en: Smooth tissue that cushions bones in a joint
words.example_en: Small-molecule drugs and biologics can also wash out of synovial fluid fast, limiting how much medicine actually reaches damaged cartilage.
